newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't denies bank sale is election stunt.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't denies bank sale is election stunt.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez Monday defended the planned sale of state mortgage lender Banco Hipotecario against charges that it is an "electioneering" stunt.

The criticisms have been led by Fernandez's predecessor Domingo Cavallo, sacked last July and now a harsh critic, who said last week the use of the proceeds for public works would be a "grave error...with clearly electoral aims."
But Fernandez told foreign correspondents: "I will not stop the sale of Banco Hipotecario just because the opposition says it's an election stunt."
Hipotecario has the largest assets of any Argentine bank at $4.31 billion and its privatization has been valued at up to $3.0 billion.

The draft bill, due to be debated in the lower house of Congress Tuesday, foresees spending that money on public works and social programs, rather than reducing the country's public debt as demanded by Cavallo and other critics.

Fernandez said the Hipotecario privatization was first floated in government last July or August, before economic recovery was consolidated and when it was thought such a sale would kick-start the economy.
"With time we came to an election year and today it looks like we are selling off a bank to win the vote. That is totally false," said Fernandez.
"Beyond what we do with the money, we believe privatizing Banco Hipotecario is an excellent idea. It will give dynamism to the home loans market in Argentina," said the minister.
